summary: Gerstner argues that 90% of SaaS stocks deserve to be down because AI is permanently compressing their terminal value multiples — even if revenues remain stable, the available profit pool is shrinking as value migrates to the agentic layer.
quote: 90% of them deserve to be down... it's never gonna trade at 30 times free cash flow again. And it's going to trade 17 times free cash flow because its available TAM in the future is now dramatically and permanently changed.

summary: Sacks believes the 'all SaaS is dead' narrative is overstated for entrenched systems like Salesforce, but sees a real threat that value capture shifts to a new agentic layer on top of existing SaaS, compressing future opportunity for these companies.
quote: I think this like very dire prediction of all SaaS is dead is overstated. However... the risk for the SaaS companies... it's that they become an old layer of the stack that now there's a new layer that gets built on top of.

summary: Sacks argues Salesforce won't be ripped out and replaced by AI-generated code given its deeply tested, enterprise-vetted codebase, but acknowledges its future value capture is at risk as the agentic layer may supersede its AI ambitions.
quote: You take a SaaS product like Salesforce, right? It's a very large system... The idea that you're just going to rip out that system and replace it with code that's been probabilistically generated by an AI engine yesterday... just doesn't

summary: Gerstner argues Salesforce's multiple compression from 30x to 15x free cash flow is justified by AI-driven TAM uncertainty and the company will only re-rate higher if it can demonstrably accelerate revenue growth and prove it is an AI beneficiary.
quote: it's gone from 30 times free cash flow multiple to 15 times. That means somebody buying it today says, listen, I think 15 years into the future I can count on these free cash flows

summary: Gerstner highlights Databricks as a clear AI beneficiary within software, citing three consecutive quarters of reaccelerating growth above 60% at scale, driven by the fact that all AI tools rely on data transformation that runs through its platform.
quote: I'll tell you a company that is doing this, Databricks. Databricks just reaccelerated the last 3 quarters. They're growing over 60% at scale. Snowflake reaccelerating. ClickHouse reaccelerating. There are beneficiaries in the software

summary: Jason names Amazon as his top pick for the company of the future, arguing AI-driven efficiency will allow it to dramatically increase output with fewer people, making it extraordinarily more profitable.
quote: a company like Amazon, which is like my number one pick for like the company of the future. They're going to be able to do so much more with so many fewer people. It's extraordinary.

summary: Gerstner is enthusiastic about the SpaceX-xAI merger, arguing it combines the two largest TAMs in the world — all of AI and all of space — under the world's greatest entrepreneur, with massive retail and institutional demand to invest in that combined vision including Starlink growth and space-based data centers.
quote: You're merging the two biggest TAMs in the world, right? All of artificial intelligence. And all of space together with the world's greatest entrepreneur. And he said... I'm gonna have data centers in space in 30 months

summary: Jason believes the SpaceX-xAI merger is an extraordinary over-the-top move that will work given Elon's unmatched execution ability, and frames it as a transformational change to the AI and space landscape.
quote: he has figured it out. I've sat with him and he's, he's walked me through it, like how this works. It works. So the question is simply execution. There is no stronger entrepreneur when it comes to execution. In the history of entrepreneurs
